99.title: Build the shared CanvasSpec renderer and MCP App View foundation
99.body:
Parent: #93. Related: #71. Depends on #80, #94, #95, #97, and #98. Establish the versioned semantic Canvas renderer and separate MCP App View artifact that #71 will consume.

## Research-backed execution amendment — 2026-10-09

The original scope and discussion remain in force. Interpret the dependencies above as the **specific consumed foundation contracts**, not a requirement that every umbrella/quality issue close before a bounded renderer can be implemented. #101 owns execution; preserve existing owners and shared-file integration policy.

### Product and ownership boundary

The MCP Apps SDK supplies the View/host bridge, hooks and resource/tool helpers. It does **not** supply Actions' semantic CanvasSpec renderer, generated Python backend, revision builder or durable application state. This issue owns the renderer/View and host adapters; #100 owns the lightweight public authoring/serialization contract; #71 owns the foundry and consumes common Runtime lifecycle services. Do not introduce a second MCP server, queue, Package system or agent reasoning loop.

At inspected source `ab9b1aaa95aacc3b40c23e4fcd4749c79e3fae47`, `apps/canvas-view/src/main.tsx` is a placeholder. Passing the existing dual build proves an artifact boundary, not an interactive Canvas product.

### 99-A — portable MCP App and minimal semantic renderer

- Use the stable MCP Apps wire contract (`2026-01-26`) and official `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` bridge. ext-apps 2.x has different TypeScript dependencies/APIs but does not constitute a new Apps wire protocol. Pin and test the actual dependency/Node/Zod/TS-SDK combination; do not blindly copy SDK-v1 examples into a v2 workspace.
- Preserve separate Runtime-admin and Canvas View artifacts, shared owned UI primitives and #98's offline inventory/SBOM/build validation.
- With #100, make one bounded rendering-reuse decision: thin owned renderer, json-render's catalog/React facilities, or a compatible A2UI profile. Existing primary sources demonstrate semantic UI + MCP Apps; do not assume this layer must be invented. Do not require all alternatives or migrate the Runtime shell. Prove the selected approach on one small fixture and record any incompatible SDK peers, draft APIs, CSP or bundle constraints.
- Start with enough components for one useful app: semantic layout, form, table/result view, validation/errors and artifact/status controls. Richer archetypes remain retained scope, not prerequisites to proving the first round trip.
- Validate schema/version, allowed component/action vocabulary, bindings, input size/depth and resource references. Unknown required capabilities fail clearly. No raw generated JavaScript, eval, arbitrary URLs/paths, or schema-supplied server/tool authority.
- Serve the versioned/cache-safe `ui://action-canvas/...` HTML resource; keep application state in tool results or authorized app calls, not user-specific cached HTML. Preserve complete result metadata. UI-only resources need `resources/read` support, not mandatory `resources/list` exposure.
- Use the standard `ui/initialize` View handshake and negotiated host capabilities. This is separate from core MCP 2026-07-28's sessionless server protocol.
- App-only dispatch must validate Workspace, app, immutable revision/Deployment, binding, input and idempotency against server-owned policy. Visibility metadata, a client-supplied app ID, and possession of an artifact digest are not authorization.
- Maintain text/headless fallback and a Runtime-preview adapter over the same renderer/services. No host-specific runtime fork.

### 99-B — ChatGPT-native host projection, not a portable-core prerequisite

Consume OpenAI MCP Extensions through a thin host adapter and demonstrated capability/version support. Add a **read-only, empty-input launcher** for the app library/current app (name such as `canvas_open` is illustrative), eligible for global/thread entrypoints. Opening, remounting or deep-linking must not create an app, apply a revision, publish, or rerun an Action. Use the supplied initial tool result instead of repeating the initial call.

The extension specification requires `{}` for global/thread entrypoints and says `ui.visibility` is ignored for entrypoint invocation. Consequently, do not attach entrypoints directly to effectful `canvas_create`, `canvas_apply` or `canvas_release`. Keep the catalog bounded; route among generated apps inside a stable launcher/resource instead of registering one entrypoint/tool per app.

Validate deep links as navigation only and reauthorize the selected app/revision. Implement model-context selection, replacement, remount restoration and explicit clearing without copying secrets or bulk data into the transcript. `_meta` is not a secrets vault. Avoid cross-thread app-state leakage.

Desktop/Work-browser/mobile support must be recorded separately; the published OpenAI table is launch-scoped and excludes classic ChatGPT. File handlers, composer mentions, rich forms and deep links have differing support. They are optional follow-ons, not assumed universal capabilities. Defer unused surfaces rather than add placeholder success.

### Acceptance additions

- [ ] One reference app renders through both Runtime preview and an MCP Apps host harness; a user interaction invokes a real public-authored Python Action and changes the displayed result.
- [ ] Exact source, schema, bundle digest, server/SDK/host versions and authentic network/tool receipts accompany screenshots.
- [ ] Standard bridge, unsupported-host fallback, wrong/missing resource, bad schema/binding, malformed result, denied access and backend failure are tested.
- [ ] CSP/offline loading, keyboard/focus, responsive layouts, loading/empty/error states and bounded large-result handling pass on the actual packaged artifact.
- [ ] Cross-app/revision substitution and unauthorized app-only calls fail; retry/remount does not duplicate effects.
- [ ] ChatGPT global/thread open, deep-link, context-clear/remount tests have explicit PASS/BLOCKED/NOT RUN by actual host. Harness success is not a real ChatGPT support claim.
- [ ] #99 remains separate from #71 persistence/revision-builder/generated-backend acceptance and #127 template packaging.

### Primary references

- https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/blob/main/specification/2026-01-26/apps.mdx
- https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/releases
- https://github.com/openai/mcp-extensions/blob/main/docs/spec.md
- https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/extensions
- https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render
- https://json-render.dev/docs/api/mcp
- https://a2ui.org/guides/a2ui-in-mcp-apps/

100.title: Define Canvas authoring contracts in actions-core without package proliferation
100.body:
Parent: #93. Related: #71 and #99. Decide and implement the smallest Python authoring surface needed for Canvas while keeping runtime behavior in actions-runtime and avoiding a speculative new distribution.

## Research-backed execution amendment — 2026-10-09

This amendment preserves the original issue and all discussion/acceptance history. It refines the existing Canvas lane; it is not a new campaign, a completion claim, or permission to replace an active owner. #101 remains execution authority. The 2026-10-09 19:09Z CAS receipt records **Cloud E owning #100** and a reserved, undispatched Devsy Canvas worktree. Reconcile live ownership before changing that assignment.

### Current evidence and scope

PR #254 (`docs/issue-100-authoring-decision-20261009`, observed head `a4946a297d8fce4b95a7a2147db6d7569c6463ae`) is a proposed ADR, not an implemented authoring API or schema. At its inspected integration base `ab9b1aaa95aacc3b40c23e4fcd4749c79e3fae47`, public `actions.mcp.tool` still rejects additional metadata kwargs; internal `Action.options` preservation is not public authoring acceptance. Continue/adapt this work rather than create a competing ADR or package.

### Two separately accepted deliverables

**100-A — supported public MCP Apps authoring.** Define the smallest serializable, validated `actions-core/actions.mcp` contract for tool UI association (`_meta.ui.resourceUri`), model/app visibility, and corresponding UI resources with `ui://` identity and `text/html;profile=mcp-app`. Runtime owns server registration, resource delivery, policy and SDK adaptation. Resource metadata/CSP and complete result `content`, `structuredContent` and `_meta` must survive the real adapter. An ordinary Action author must not import the Canvas renderer, Runtime, React, or OpenAI host SDK.

A UI resource must be retrievable through `resources/read` at the advertised URI. The stable Apps specification permits UI-only resources to be omitted from `resources/list`; do not accidentally require catalog exposure as an interoperability rule. App-only visibility is a host/catalog routing declaration, **not** authorization for arbitrary backend operations.

**100-B — canonical CanvasSpec serialization.** Retain one versioned JSON Schema artifact as the proposed Python/TypeScript interchange source of truth. #99 owns semantic components/layout/state/UI-binding fields jointly with this contract; #71 and #129/#130/#87/#131/#132 own backend identity and provider semantics. A schema artifact does not itself imply a new PyPI/npm distribution. Reject unknown required versions/features, bound size/depth/reference resolution, and define compatibility and round-trip behavior.

Before freezing a bespoke semantic grammar, record one bounded reuse decision with #99: existing owned components plus a thin renderer versus json-render catalogs/React renderer versus an A2UI profile. Run the same small fixture through the selected approach and explain dependency, offline/CSP, accessibility, Python interchange, typed dispatch, license, and MCP-SDK compatibility tradeoffs. This is **not** a requirement to build three renderers or pause unrelated work for an open-ended survey. Canvas remains an Actions-owned product even when a rendering library is reused.

### Dependency semantics — prevent false blocking

- #93 and #101 are parent/coordination relationships, not prerequisites requiring those umbrellas to close before this child starts.
- The blanket historical `deferred behind #125` wording is replaced by **criterion-level prerequisite receipts**: verify the relevant public-dependency, Core/Runtime packaging, template/artifact and MCP regression boundaries on the actual candidate. Do not waive unproved security/packaging requirements; do not wait for unrelated #125 rows or recreate merged PR #128.
- 100-A can be proved with a tiny hand-authored MCP App and does not require the complete Canvas foundry or renderer.
- 100-B and #99 may iterate against one agreed fixture/schema checkpoint with disjoint ownership; neither requires the other's entire issue to be closed first.
- #127 consumes accepted authoring and renderer slices. #71 consumes those plus the common backend lifecycle; neither is a prerequisite for 100-A.

### Acceptance additions (original acceptance remains)

- [ ] Public-decorator/package fixture, not manually populated internal `Action.options`, reaches `tools/list` and `resources/read` through the actual Runtime adapter.
- [ ] UI association, visibility, MIME, resource metadata/CSP, and result metadata round-trip; malformed/unknown metadata and missing/wrong resources fail truthfully.
- [ ] Python → JSON → TypeScript and reverse fixture validation agrees at an exact schema revision; unsupported versions/features and oversized/pathological inputs are rejected.
- [ ] Reuse decision is backed by the small working fixture, not library marketing. SDK peer compatibility is checked against repository lockfiles before adoption.
- [ ] Normal `@action` installation/import remains lightweight; wheel/sdist and dependency/package-size receipts demonstrate no frontend/Runtime/OpenAI dependency leakage.
- [ ] Protocol version, Python MCP SDK version, MCP Apps wire version, ext-apps package version and CanvasSpec version are recorded separately.
- [ ] ADR review, implementation, packaged verification and host acceptance are distinct statuses; merging PR #254 cannot close #100 by itself.

### Primary references (checked 2026-10-09)

- Stable MCP Apps contract: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/blob/main/specification/2026-01-26/apps.mdx
- ext-apps releases and 2.x migration boundary: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/releases
- OpenAI host extensions: https://github.com/openai/mcp-extensions/blob/main/docs/spec.md
- json-render authoring/renderer: https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render and https://json-render.dev/docs/api/mcp
- A2UI current/candidate distinction and MCP Apps integration: https://a2ui.org/ and https://a2ui.org/guides/a2ui-in-mcp-apps/
- Observed owner receipt: https://github.com/joshyorko/actions/blob/cf883d45c9ebc125cfaeabe247496222720ba408/docs/program/evidence/cas-expansion-20261009-1909.json

126.title: feat: add an MCP v2 capabilities showcase template
126.body:
Execution parent: #93 / #101. Current state: stateless MCP v2 is shipped, but this showcase template is not implemented. PR #128 cleanup is merged; reconcile only actual remaining #125 acceptance relevant to the template rather than waiting for an obsolete cleanup branch.

## Goal

Design and later implement a community-owned template that showcases the full supported MCP v2 surface of Action Server.

## Status

Open implementation/design track. No showcase template is shipped yet; use the current public package contracts and verify the relevant remaining cleanup acceptance.

## Capabilities to demonstrate

- Stateless MCP `2026-07-28` discovery and per-request calls at `/mcp`.
- Tools, resources, resource templates, and prompts.
- Typed inputs/outputs and structured content.
- Catalog revision and immediate-staleness metadata behavior.
- Request metadata/correlation boundaries and safe error handling.
- Streaming/SSE lifecycle safety without initialization/session-era compatibility.
- Public dependencies only and offline-capable template packaging.

## Acceptance direction

- Separate branch and approved design/spec.
- Deterministic generated bundle integration.
- End-to-end client examples and protocol boundary tests.
- No Sema4AI product services, private packages, legacy `/sse`, or initialization/session compatibility.
- Documentation clearly distinguishes protocol capabilities from product-specific integrations.

## Dependency

Depends on verified public-package/template boundaries from #125; the merged cleanup PR is not an outstanding implementation dependency.

## Protocol and Canvas separation — 2026-10-09 research amendment

Preserve the existing #219 design/checkpoint and reconcile its current status before starting another writer. #93/#101 are execution parents, not prerequisites that must close before this child can proceed. #71/#99/#100/#127 are related Canvas work, not a requirement to complete the foundry before demonstrating the core protocol.

Add an exact-version capability matrix to the example/evidence: core MCP protocol, locked Python MCP SDK, installed extensions, demonstrated Runtime behavior and host support. A specification or installed SDK feature is not proof that Actions exposes a supported public API for it.

- Core `2026-07-28` requires servers to implement `server/discover`; clients may choose whether to call it. Demonstrate stateless calls, required request/result metadata, routing and errors through the actual mounted Runtime.
- Keep the core server protocol separate from MCP Apps' `ui/initialize` handshake. A UI handshake must not be rejected by a blanket assertion that every kind of initialization is obsolete.
- Tasks are an official extension rather than core functionality. Do not claim durable Tasks/Canvas jobs from the SDK major version alone; #85/#92 must supply the real Run-backed implementation and acceptance before such examples are advertised.
- Demonstrate MRTR or other optional interactions only when actually implemented and supported. Preserve semantic-operation idempotency across retries; a protocol request ID is not a durable effect key.
- Do not introduce new dependencies on deprecated roots/sampling/logging just to make the showcase look exhaustive. Record unsupported/unimplemented cells honestly.
- Keep cacheable renderer/catalog metadata separate from authorized per-user application state; no public caching of private data.
- MCP Apps authoring/template proof remains with #100/#99/#127; new ChatGPT entrypoints are optional host projection, not a core-protocol feature named Canvas.

Acceptance adds a fresh packaged client/server trace for every advertised cell and explicit NOT RUN/UNSUPPORTED classifications. No global #125 closure or host extension rollout is required where the concrete public-package/template prerequisites are proven.

Primary sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog and https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/blob/main/specification/2026-01-26/apps.mdx

127.title: feat: add a community Canvas template
127.body:
Execution parent: #93 / #101. Product direction: #71. Required implementation dependencies: #99 (Canvas renderer/MCP App View) and #100 (Python authoring contract in actions-core). Current Canvas View is a placeholder; this template must demonstrate a real working renderer, not imply Canvas is already usable.

## Goal

Design and later implement a community-owned Action Server template that demonstrates the existing Canvas frontend/runtime boundary without depending on Sema4AI products, private registries, paid services, or vendor-only packages.

## Status

Open design/template track; implement after the #99/#100 authoring/rendering contract can be exercised. PR #128 cleanup is merged; verify relevant remaining #125 acceptance on current community.

## Design requirements

- Separate branch and design/spec review.
- Public dependencies only; offline-capable packaging.
- Preserve the existing independent Runtime and Canvas Vite roots.
- Define the user journey, action-to-canvas data contract, CSP/offline constraints, accessibility, responsive behavior, and testable example.
- Integrate through the deterministic template manifest/bundle generator.
- Include template creation, package execution, frontend build, and contract tests.
- Do not reintroduce product tiering, private registries, hosted service assumptions, or Sema4AI-specific configuration.

## Dependency

Blocked by working #99/#100 authoring/rendering contracts; preserve verified #125 public-dependency and offline template boundaries.

## Dependency-cycle correction and vertical acceptance — 2026-10-09

**#71 is product direction, not a prerequisite that must complete before this template. #93 and #101 are coordination/acceptance umbrellas, not implementation blockers.** The 19:20Z operational graph in PR #220 incorrectly lists #71/#93/#101 as unresolved prerequisites for #127 while #71 itself waits on #127. Correct that machine-readable projection without erasing the original requirement records or historical snapshots.

The true template readiness gate is the accepted **100-A public authoring + 100-B serialization + 99-A renderer/bridge slices**, plus the concrete consumed #125 public-package/template and #98 artifact criteria. No requirement to finish all #71 foundry behavior, native ChatGPT extensions, distributed workers, or close #93/#101 first.

### Smallest useful template proof

Use one bounded, credential-free example, preferably reusing the reference fixture agreed by #99/#100 rather than starting a second design. It must exercise a typed Python Action, a real form/result interaction, clear validation/backend errors and a retrievable result/artifact. A local data-review/form-table-export example is a candidate, not a mandated new domain subsystem. Do not use synthetic live swarm metrics or provision external infrastructure merely to demonstrate UI.

The template is hand-authored reference packaging. It proves a supported way to author and run an MCP App; it **does not prove** that a prompt can create a new backend, safely activate revisions or roll back. Those remain separate #71 gates.

### Additional acceptance

- [ ] Canonical template manifest/bundle generation produces deterministic public-only archives; fresh creation succeeds with documented offline/preseeded assumptions.
- [ ] A fresh package installs the real public `actions.mcp` authoring contract; no internal metadata injection or hand-edited generated bundle.
- [ ] The package runs in the actual source/wheel/frozen Runtime modes being claimed, serves the expected UI resource, and completes a genuine Python tool → rendered result → user interaction → backend result round trip.
- [ ] Runtime preview and MCP Apps host-harness evidence identify exact versions/digests; real ChatGPT evidence is recorded separately when available.
- [ ] Unsupported host, denied operation, invalid form input, backend error, missing artifact and retry/remount states remain truthful; text fallback works.
- [ ] No dependency on completion of the parent umbrella or #71 is encoded into the scheduling DAG; parent completion may still aggregate this child.
- [ ] Template acceptance, generated-app foundry acceptance and ChatGPT-native extension acceptance remain separate ledger rows.

References: #99 and #100 research-backed amendments; https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/blob/main/specification/2026-01-26/apps.mdx
